```{r setup}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# National Data — single-topic downloadable view
#
# This template is rendered on demand by the National Data Shiny app when the
# user clicks "Download Selected Topic". All substantive content (map, table,
# titles, notes) is prepared by the app and passed in via a single RDS bundle
# so this document only handles presentation and ADA-PARC branding. Keeping the
# data logic in the app is the single source of truth: what downloads always
# matches what is on screen.
#
# Bundle contents (see server downloadHandler in ADA_PARC.Rmd):
#   title         cleaned topic title (character)
#   category      category label, e.g. "Demographics" (character)
#   interp_note   interpretation note or "" (character)
#   source_note   data source sentence (character)
#   universe_note population / denominator sentence or "" (character)
#   column_defs   data.frame(term, definition) for the % columns; 0 rows = omit
#   alt_text      plain-language map summary for accessibility (character)
#   table_df      formatted data frame, first column "State" (data.frame)
#   map_svg       the state map as inline SVG markup (character)
#   generated     date string (character)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
options(cli.width = 80)

library(htmltools)
library(knitr)

b <- tryCatch(readRDS(params$bundle), error = function(e) NULL)

ok <- !is.null(b) &&
  all(c("title", "table_df", "map_svg") %in% names(b))

# Small helpers with safe fallbacks
val <- function(name, default = "") {
  if (ok && !is.null(b[[name]]) && length(b[[name]]) == 1 &&
      !is.na(b[[name]]) && nzchar(trimws(b[[name]]))) b[[name]] else default
}

# Audit finding C4, 2026-08-26: this table was previously knitr::kable(...,
# format = "html"), whose HTML writer never adds a scope attribute to a
# <thead> th and never emits a <caption> unless a caption string is
# supplied and styled for it. city_profile.qmd's tables avoid both gaps by
# building the markup directly (render_comparison_table() in ADA_PARC.Rmd);
# this does the same for an arbitrary-width data grid rather than a fixed
# with/without-disability pair.
#
# caption is visually hidden (.sr-only, defined in the {css} block below):
# each table page already carries a visible <h2 class="section-title"> with
# the same title text directly above it (see the page-two chunk), and a
# second visible caption repeating that text would just be noise for a
# sighted reader. A screen reader user still gets the table's name announced
# because the <caption> is programmatically tied to the <table>, which a
# preceding heading never is.
#
# No inline alignment: table.national-table's CSS already right-aligns every
# column but the first (thead th:not(:first-child), tbody td default vs.
# tbody td:first-child), so there is nothing left for a per-cell style to do.
render_national_table <- function(df, caption) {
  esc <- htmltools::htmlEscape

  header_cells <- paste0(
    '<th scope="col">', vapply(names(df), esc, character(1)), '</th>',
    collapse = ""
  )

  row_html <- function(row) {
    cells <- vapply(row, function(x) esc(as.character(x)), character(1))
    paste0("<tr>", paste0("<td>", cells, "</td>", collapse = ""), "</tr>")
  }
  body_rows <- apply(df, 1, row_html)

  paste0(
    '<table class="national-table">',
    '<caption class="sr-only">', esc(caption), '</caption>',
    "<thead><tr>", header_cells, "</tr></thead>",
    "<tbody>", paste0(body_rows, collapse = ""), "</tbody>",
    "</table>"
  )
}
```

```{css}
:root {

  --adaparc-gold:   #c9a84c;
  --adaparc-ink:    #1c2b3a;
}

body {
  font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;

  font-size: 18px;
  line-height: 1.5;

  margin: 0 auto;
  padding: 0 0.5in 0.75in 0.5in;
}

/* ── Brand banner ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

  border-bottom: 5px solid var(--adaparc-gold);

}

}

}
.adaparc-banner .sub {

/* ── Interpretation note ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

}

/* ── Map figure ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.map-figure { margin: 0.5rem 0 1rem 0; text-align: center; }
.map-figure svg { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }

/* ── Understanding This Data (mirrors the on-screen card) ────────────────── */
/* Its own page in print / "Save as PDF"; just a section break on screen.
   Slate/navy chrome to match the site: navy left bar on each section panel,
   very light panel fill so text keeps maximum contrast, navy icon chips. */
.understanding {
  margin: 1.25rem 0 0 0;
  break-before: page;
  page-break-before: always;
}
.understanding .section-title { margin-bottom: 0.15rem; }
.ud-rule {
  width: 64px;
  height: 4px;
  background: var(--adaparc-gold);
  border-radius: 2px;
  margin: 0.55rem 0 0 0;
}
.ud-block {
  margin-top: 1.15rem;
  background: #f6f8fb;
  border: 1px solid #d5dee8;
  border-left: 4px solid var(--adaparc-ink);
  border-radius: 6px;
  padding: 1.15rem 1.3rem;
}
.ud-subhead {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.65rem;
  font-size: 1.15rem;
  font-weight: 700;

}
.ud-chip {

}

/* ── Data table ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.table-wrap { margin-top: 0.5rem; overflow-x: auto; }
table.national-table {
  border-collapse: collapse;

}
table.national-table thead th {

}
table.national-table tbody tr:nth-child(even) { background: #f6f3ee; }
table.national-table thead th:not(:first-child) { text-align: right; }

/* Screen-reader-only table caption. See render_national_table() in the
   setup chunk (audit finding C4, 2026-08-26). */
.sr-only {
  position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding: 0; margin: -1px;
  overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0,0,0,0); white-space: nowrap; border: 0;
}

/* ── Footer ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.adaparc-footer {
  margin-top: 1.5rem;
  padding-top: 0.75rem;
  border-top: 2px solid var(--adaparc-gold);
  font-size: 0.9rem;
  color: #555;
}
.adaparc-footer p { margin: 0.2rem 0; }
.adaparc-footer .funding-note {
  font-weight: 600;
  color: var(--adaparc-ink);
}

/* ── "See next page" note ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.see-next {
  margin: 1.25rem 0 0 0;
  font-size: 1rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  color: var(--adaparc-maroon);
}

/* ── Screen-only print helper ─────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.print-bar {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.85rem;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  margin: 0 0 1rem 0;
}
.btn-print {
  font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
  font-size: 1.05rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  color: #ffffff;
  background: var(--adaparc-maroon);
  border: 1.5px solid var(--adaparc-maroon);
  border-radius: 6px;
  padding: 8px 18px;
  cursor: pointer;
}
.btn-print:hover { background: #8b2737; border-color: #8b2737; }
.btn-print:focus { outline: 3px solid var(--adaparc-gold); outline-offset: 2px; }

/* ── Pagination: map on page 1, table from page 2 ─────────────────────────── */
/* An explicit page box gives print/PDF engines a defined page size so the
   break below is actually paginated (without @page, some "save to PDF" paths
   lay the whole document on one continuous page and ignore the break). */
@page {
  size: Letter;
  margin: 0.6in 0.5in;
}
.page-two {
  break-before: page;
  page-break-before: always;
}

@media print {
  /* Quarto wraps the document in #quarto-content.page-columns, which is a CSS
     grid, and main.content is one of its grid items. Chromium does not
     fragment grid containers: it lays the whole grid out monolithically and
     drops forced breaks inside it, which is why "Save as PDF" was returning a
     single clipped page. Restoring normal block layout for print puts the
     document back on the standard fragmentation path so @page and
     .page-two are honored. */
  #quarto-content,
  #quarto-content.page-columns,
  .page-columns,
  main.content,
  main#quarto-document-content,
  .cell {
    display: block !important;
    grid-template-columns: none !important;
  }

  .print-bar { display: none !important; }

  body { max-width: none; padding: 0; font-size: 12pt; }

  /* Backgrounds carry meaning here (brand banner, table header, zebra rows),
     so ask the engine to print them rather than drop them. */
  body,
  .adaparc-banner,
  table.national-table thead th,
  table.national-table tbody tr:nth-child(even) {
    -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact;
    print-color-adjust: exact;
  }

  /* Page one budget: banner, title, interpretation note, map and summary have
     to clear 9.8in of content box. The map is exported at 9 x 6.4in, so
     unconstrained it renders ~5.3in tall and pushes the closing line onto a
     stray page of its own. Fixing its printed height (width follows from the
     viewBox aspect ratio) leaves room for the summary below it. Population,
     source and definitions no longer sit here - they are on their own page
     after the table - so the map keeps its fuller height. */
  .adaparc-banner { padding: 0.7rem 1rem; margin-bottom: 0.8rem; }
  .adaparc-banner .banner-icon { height: 30px; }
  h1.topic-title { font-size: 17pt; margin: 0 0 0.45rem 0; }
  .interp-note { margin-bottom: 0.6rem; padding: 0.5rem 0.8rem; }
  .map-figure { margin: 0.3rem 0 0.5rem 0; }
  .map-figure svg {
    height: 4.3in !important;
    width: auto !important;
    max-width: 100% !important;
  }
  .map-summary { margin-top: 0.3rem; }
  .see-next { margin-top: 0.6rem; break-inside: avoid; }

  /* Understanding This Data: its own page (break-before set outside the media
     query). Keep each panel and each term/definition pair from splitting, and
     ask the engine to keep the navy accents / panel fills. */
  .understanding .section-title { break-after: avoid; }
  .ud-block,
  .ud-defs-note {
    break-inside: avoid;
    -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact;
    print-color-adjust: exact;
  }
  .ud-defs { font-size: 9pt; }
  .ud-def { break-inside: avoid; }

  /* Page two onward: 52 rows of five columns will not fit on a single sheet at
     a readable size, so the table flows across two pages with the column
     header repeated and no row split across the break.

     The wrapper has to drop its horizontal scroll first. Any ancestor with a
     non-visible overflow is a monolithic fragmentation context in Chromium:
     the table cannot be split, so the overflow is clipped at the page edge
     (the "cut off" rows) and the header group is never re-emitted on the
     following page. Bootstrap's .cell-output-display and .table-responsive
     carry the same overflow-x, so they are reset alongside .table-wrap. */
  .table-wrap,
  .cell-output-display,
  .knitsql-table,
  .table-responsive,
  .page-two {
    overflow: visible !important;
  }

  /* Each block is one printed page of the table, carrying its own header. */
  .table-page-next {
    break-before: page;
    page-break-before: always;
  }
  .table-page { break-inside: auto; }

  h2.section-title { font-size: 14pt; break-after: avoid; }
  h2.section-title-continued { font-size: 12pt; }
  table.national-table { font-size: 9.5pt; break-inside: auto; }
  table.national-table thead th { padding: 4px 8px; }
  table.national-table tbody td { padding: 2px 8px; }
  /* Explicit groups: the header repeats on every page the table spans, and
     the body stays a normal fragmentable row group. */
  table.national-table thead { display: table-header-group !important; }
  table.national-table tbody { display: table-row-group !important; }
  table.national-table tr {
    break-inside: avoid;
    page-break-inside: avoid;
  }
  .adaparc-footer {
    break-inside: avoid;
    font-size: 8pt;
    margin-top: 0.5rem;
    padding-top: 0.35rem;
  }
  .adaparc-footer p { margin: 0.1rem 0; }
  a[href]:after { content: ""; }
}
```

```{r banner, results='asis'}
if (!ok) {
  cat('<div class="adaparc-banner"><p class="brand">ADA-PARC</p>',
      '<p class="sub">National Data</p></div>',
      '<p>No topic was provided to render. Please return to the ',
      'National Data page and try again.</p>')
  knitr::knit_exit()
}

# Built as a plain string, not htmltools tag objects: piping htmltools tags
# through as.character() into a results='asis' chunk lets Quarto's Markdown
# layer round-trip the markup as text instead of passing it through as raw
# HTML (that's what printed literally on the page). Every other chunk in this
# file already builds HTML this way; the banner is now consistent with them.
cat(paste0(
  '<div class="adaparc-banner">',
  '<div class="banner-content">',
  '<div>',
  '<p class="brand">ADA-PARC</p>',
  '<p class="sub">National Data',
  if (nzchar(val("category"))) paste0("  ·  ", htmltools::htmlEscape(val("category"))) else "",
  '</p>',
  '</div>',
  # Same white knockout mark used on the fact sheet banner, so the two
  # download types share one brand asset even though their layouts stay
  # distinct. Decorative (alt="") because the adjacent "ADA-PARC" text
  # already names the organization for screen readers. Placed last so
  # justify-content: space-between puts it at the right edge, clear of the
  # title text.
  '<img class="banner-icon" src="../www/brand/PARC_white_icon_knockout.png" alt="">',
  '</div>',
  '</div>\n'
))
```

```{r page-one, results='asis'}
# appears in the saved PDF. The background-graphics tip matters because the
# banner, table header and zebra rows are colour-coded.
cat(paste0(
  '<div class="print-bar">',
  '<button type="button" class="btn-print" onclick="window.print()">',
  'Print or save as PDF</button>',
  '</div>\n'
))

# Topic title
cat(sprintf('<h1 class="topic-title">%s</h1>\n', htmltools::htmlEscape(val("title"))))

# Interpretation note (only present for directional indicators)
if (nzchar(val("interp_note"))) {
  cat(sprintf(
    '<div class="interp-note"><span class="label">Interpretation Note: </span>%s</div>\n',
    htmltools::htmlEscape(val("interp_note"))
  ))
}

# Map (inline SVG, already contains the legend/key)
cat('<div class="map-figure" role="img" aria-label="',
    htmltools::htmlEscape(val("alt_text", "State-by-state map of the selected topic."), attribute = TRUE),
    '">\n', sep = "")
cat(b$map_svg)
cat('\n</div>\n')

# Accessible plain-language summary
if (nzchar(val("alt_text"))) {
  cat(sprintf(
    '<p class="map-summary"><span class="label">Summary: </span>%s</p>\n',
    htmltools::htmlEscape(val("alt_text"))
  ))
}

# Population examined, data source and column definitions have moved to the
# "Understanding This Data" section after the table (see the page-two chunk),
# mirroring the on-screen card. Page one is just the map and its summary now.

# End-of-page-one pointer to the table, which starts on page 2
cat('<p class="see-next">Data table begins on the next page.</p>\n')
```

```{r page-two, results='asis'}
# ── Data table, split into one table per printed page ───────────────────────
# A single long table with one <thead> relies on the print engine repeating
# the header group on continuation pages. Chromium and Firefox do; WebKit
# (Safari, and therefore macOS "Export as PDF") does not, and has never
# implemented it, so the second table page arrived headerless. Emitting each
# page's rows as its own table with its own header makes the result identical
# in every engine and in any HTML-to-PDF converter, at the cost of choosing
# the split point here rather than letting the engine choose it.
#
# ROWS_PER_PAGE is the measured capacity of one Letter page at the print
# styles set above: heading + header row + rows, with the last page also
# carrying the footer. National tables run 53 rows (US, 50 states, DC, PR),
# so this yields two balanced pages of roughly 27 rows.
ROWS_PER_PAGE <- 27L

cat('<div class="page-two">\n')

df <- b$table_df
# Column alignment is CSS-driven, not passed in here; see the note on
# render_national_table() in the setup chunk.

n_rows  <- nrow(df)
n_pages <- max(1L, as.integer(ceiling(n_rows / ROWS_PER_PAGE)))
# Balance the pages rather than filling the first to capacity and leaving a
# stub on the last one.
per_page <- as.integer(ceiling(n_rows / n_pages))
groups   <- split(seq_len(n_rows), ceiling(seq_len(n_rows) / per_page))

title_esc <- htmltools::htmlEscape(val("title"))

for (k in seq_along(groups)) {
  # The first block inherits the page break from .page-two; each later block
  # carries its own.
  cat(sprintf('<div class="table-page%s">\n',
              if (k == 1) "" else " table-page-next"))

  page_title <- val("title", "State comparison")
  if (k == 1) {
    cat(sprintf('<h2 class="section-title">Data Table: %s</h2>\n', title_esc))
    table_caption <- sprintf("Data table: %s", page_title)
  } else {
    cat(sprintf(
      '<h2 class="section-title section-title-continued">Data Table: %s <span class="continued">(continued)</span></h2>\n',
      title_esc
    ))
    table_caption <- sprintf("Data table: %s (continued), page %d of %d",
                              page_title, k, length(groups))
  }

  chunk <- df[groups[[k]], , drop = FALSE]

  # render_national_table() (setup chunk) replaces the prior knitr::kable()
  # call: kable's HTML writer never scopes a <thead> th and never emits a
  # <caption>. See the audit finding C4 note there.
  tbl_html <- render_national_table(chunk, table_caption)

  cat('<div class="table-wrap">\n')
  cat(tbl_html)
  cat('\n</div>\n')
  cat('</div>\n')
}

# ── Understanding This Data ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Mirrors the on-screen card of the same name: who is counted (universe_note),
# where the numbers come from (source_note) and what each percentage column
# means (column_defs). All content is prepared app-side; this file only lays it
# out. Starts on its own page so the table is never crowded by it.
esc <- htmltools::htmlEscape

ud_chip <- function(kind) {
  p <- switch(
    kind,
    pop = '<circle cx="9" cy="8" r="3.1"/><path d="M3.7 19c0-2.9 2.4-4.8 5.3-4.8S14.3 16.1 14.3 19"/><circle cx="16.8" cy="9.6" r="2.5"/><path d="M15 14.3c2.3.2 4.3 1.9 4.3 4.7"/>',
    src = '<path d="M6 3.6h7.5L18 8.1V19.4a1 1 0 0 1-1 1H6a1 1 0 0 1-1-1V4.6a1 1 0 0 1 1-1z"/><path d="M13.3 3.6v4.6H18"/><path d="M8.4 12.4h7M8.4 15.8h7"/>',
    pct = '<path d="M6.5 17.5 17.5 6.5"/><circle cx="8.3" cy="8.3" r="2.1"/><circle cx="15.7" cy="15.7" r="2.1"/>'
  )
  sprintf(
    paste0('<span class="ud-chip" aria-hidden="true">',
           '<svg class="ud-glyph" viewBox="0 0 24 24" focusable="false">%s</svg></span>'),
    p
  )
}

ud_block <- function(kind, heading, body_html) {
  sprintf(
    '<div class="ud-block"><h3 class="ud-subhead">%s<span>%s</span></h3>%s</div>\n',
    ud_chip(kind), esc(heading), body_html
  )
}

cat('<section class="understanding">\n')
cat('<h2 class="section-title">Understanding This Data</h2>\n')
cat('<div class="ud-rule" aria-hidden="true"></div>\n')

if (nzchar(val("universe_note"))) {
  cat(ud_block("pop", "Population Examined",
              sprintf('<p class="ud-body">%s</p>', esc(val("universe_note")))))
}

cat(ud_block("src", "Data Source",
            sprintf('<p class="ud-body">%s</p>',
                    esc(val("source_note", "2020-2024 American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates")))))

cd <- b$column_defs
if (is.data.frame(cd) && nrow(cd) > 0) {
  rows <- paste0(
    '<div class="ud-def"><dt>', vapply(cd$term, esc, character(1)), '</dt>',
    '<dd>', vapply(cd$definition, esc, character(1)), '</dd></div>',
    collapse = ""
  )
  defs_html <- paste0(
    '<dl class="ud-defs">', rows, '</dl>',
    '<p class="ud-defs-note">Count columns (#) show the number of people each ',
    'percentage is based on.</p>'
  )
  cat(ud_block("pct", "What Each Percentage Column Means", defs_html))
}

cat('</section>\n')
```

```{r footer, results='asis'}
# Same funding acknowledgment wording as fs_footer() in
# factsheets/_generate/R/factsheet-functions.R, kept as a literal string here
# rather than a shared function so the two download systems stay independent
# (per Colin: national + fact sheet HTML should look distinct, not share a
# banner/footer component).
cat(sprintf(
  paste0(
    '<div class="adaparc-footer">',
    '<p class="funding-note">The ADA-PARC is funded by the National ',
    'Institute for Disability, Independent Living, and Rehabilitation ',
    'Research (NIDILRR) under grants 90DP0026 and 90DPAD0001.</p>',
    '<p>ADA-PARC  ·  ADA Participation Action Research Consortium  ·  ',
    'Generated %s. Darker map colors always indicate more opportunity.</p>',
    '</div>'
  ),
  htmltools::htmlEscape(val("generated", format(Sys.Date(), "%B %d, %Y")))
))

# Close the .page-two wrapper opened in the page-two chunk so the table and
# this footer note stay grouped on the second page.
cat('</div>\n')
```
